content.title: About
content.content: Crepe is a thin pancake made from a batter of flour, eggs, milk, and a small amount of sugar. It has a delicate texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and serves as a base for both sweet and savory fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crepes originate from France, where they are called "crêpe".
The thin batter cooks in 1–2 minutes on a hot skillet.
Traditionally served with lemon and sugar, they are also paired with fruit, chocolate, cheese, or ham.
In some regions they are known as "pancakes" or "flan", though recipes may vary.
France celebrates "La Chandeleur" (Candlemas) on February 2nd, a day dedicated to making crepes.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Crepes contain eggs, which provide a complete source of high‑quality protein.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Milk in the batter supplies calcium and vitamin D, essential for bone health.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: When prepared with minimal oil, crepes have relatively low fat levels.

items.title: Quick‑digesting carbohydrates
items.content: Flour offers a fast source of energy, making crepes a convenient breakfast.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and milk are rich in B2, B12, and folate, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Egg or milk allergy
items.content: Crepes may trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to eggs or dairy.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Thin crepes made from white flour can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Traditional crepes contain wheat, so they are unsuitable for gluten‑free diets.

items.title: Overheating oil
items.content: When frying, avoid overheating the oil to prevent formation of harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve crepes hot, rolled or folded like an envelope, with fillings such as fresh fruit, berries, chocolate sauce, cream cheese, ham, or cheese. They can be dusted with powdered sugar, drizzled with lemon juice, or topped with maple syrup.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh crepes are best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat on a dry skillet or in the microwave before serving.

pizza-cheese-with-fruit-thick-crust.title: Cheese and Fruit Pizza, Thick Crust

content.title: About
content.content: Cheese and fruit pizza on a thick crust combines the creamy melt of cheese with the sweet bite of fresh fruits such as pineapple, pear or apple, all on a fluffy yet sturdy base. This fusion style is popular in fast‑food chains and specialty pizzerias worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic “Hawaiian” pizza uses pineapple, but in many countries pears or apples are added for a local twist.
Thick‑crust dough requires a longer bake, resulting in a puffier interior and a slightly crunchy exterior.
The sweet‑salty contrast of cheese and fruit enhances flavor perception through aroma synergy.
In traditional Italian cuisine such combinations are considered non‑traditional, yet they are highly demanded in international menus.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheese provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Vitamins from fruit
items.content: Fruits add vitamin C and other antioxidants that support the immune system.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbs
items.content: Thick crust supplies complex carbohydrates that keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Cheese contributes high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: If whole‑grain flour is used in the dough, fiber content rises, benefiting digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Thick crust and cheese make the pizza calorie‑rich; portion control is advised for weight management.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to dairy proteins.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Cheese often contains significant salt, which can be a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat the pizza in an oven or microwave until the crust is golden and the cheese bubbles. Slice into portions and serve hot, optionally with a light salad or barbecue sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftover pizza in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in freezer‑safe bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to 180 °C before serving to restore crispness.
